A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study despite the revised title. The complete texts, equations, three figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the reorganization.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figures 1–2 report original perturbation and gradient-descent experiments on synthetic measures. Appendix B and Figure 3 report experiments varying projection directions.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments in Section 6 and Figures 1–2, with the projection-direction experiments retained in Appendix C and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The SW objective, particle gradient descent, and update in Equation 11 are retained. The extensions concern mathematical characterization and guarantees, without establishing a changed computational procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Gaussian, sliced-uniform, and annular targets, using the same segment, dumbbell, and sampled initial point clouds. Broader theoretical target classes do not introduce additional evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing algorithms against the particle-descent scheme. The same step-size and projection-direction variants remain; newly cited works are not experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Both retain L = 100 directions and M = 10000 target samples in Section 6, N = 100 for perturbations, and N = 1000 with 200 iterations in Figure 2. The appendix retains L = 10, 20, 40, 100 and the same direction constructions.

E4.justification: The segment/dumbbell perturbations, step-size sensitivity experiments, and direction-count/orientation analysis are unchanged. The latter moves from Appendix B to Appendix C without new experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its original experiments.

E6.justification: All three figure images are identical, and their reported findings are retained: segment instability, rapid early descent near lambda = dN, divergence above 2dN, and direction-dependent local smoothness. No empirical result entries or values change.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.1 extends differentiability from integer p >= 2 to all real p >= 2 and adds gradient continuity. Proposition 3.3 expands collision-free steps from (0, Nd/2) to (0, Nd), without requiring bounded projected densities for that guarantee. New Appendix B.4 develops general-target extensions and weaker separation assumptions. Section 4 generalizes the standing target-density assumption while explicitly specifying atomlessness for relevant results. Proposition 5.1(b) and its proof correct the exponent defining alpha_d from 3/2 to 1.

C1.justification: The abstract and central critical-point contributions remain. The introduction explicitly limits the segment-instability claim to dimension two, and the conclusion broadens the stated target scope from probability densities to probability measures.

C2.justification: V2 newly discusses how atomless-target assumptions limit applications with discrete targets, explains applicability to distributions on lower-dimensional manifolds, and interprets the discretized-target experiments as suggesting practical relevance. The dimensional and perturbation restrictions were already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: V1 promises that code will become public; v2 supplies a specific repository link and states that code is available in Section 6, footnote 5. Experimental implementation settings otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds EigenVI and Li and Moosmueller, explicitly relating the latter's condition to barycentric Lagrangian criticality in Remark 4.3. It also qualifies the scope of Sarrazin's definition. The updated Tanguy references identify the same previously cited works.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, refines the introductory particle-dynamics framing, and expands the renamed Conclusion. Appendices are reorganized into auxiliary results, proofs, and numerical approximation; the atomless-projection proof is relocated. Most existing exposition and section order remain.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 retain their images, axes, legends, and captions. Figure 3 moves from a page shared with discussion to a standalone page after that discussion. The revised title, publication footer, and text reflow introduce limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical reliability through the corrected Gaussian critical-point scale and strengthens the quadratic descent/non-collision analysis beyond density targets. Clearer applicability limits and a code link also help. However, new Proposition B.9 states all p >= 2 under only a finite-second-moment target assumption, omitting the stronger moment condition needed for p > 2. The gains support a qualified overall improvement rather than an unreserved endorsement of the extensions.
